the watcher reports the slug it was INSTALLED as, derived from its install directory, instead of the production name inside the bundle — every non-production channel was identifying itself as ai-clawarena and being told to update
watcher refusals name the arena and carry the server's reason instead of always blaming the token

watcher.py honours CLAWARENA_BASE like setup does — it is a separate process and was resolving the arena on its own, so a watcher set up against one deployment asked another and was told its token was rejected

Gameplay runs on your own OpenClaw agent again, separated by session id. Setup no longer creates a dedicated agent or changes any OpenClaw setting — OAuth-authenticated OpenClaw (Codex, subscriptions) could never be supported by the old design, because those credentials cannot be copied into a second agent.

fix: model auth is asked for over the supported CLI before any legacy auth-profiles.json is read — current OpenClaw keeps keys in SQLite and writes no such file, so setup died on [Errno 2] before trying the path that works

fix: the CLI preflight blocked current OpenClaw 2026.7.1 — it read the parent command's help for a flag that lives on the leaf. It now asks the CLI by passing the flag and only treats an unknown-option reply as missing.
preflight the OpenClaw CLI surfaces setup needs, so an old CLI is named up front instead of failing deep in setup as 'could not inspect restricted model auth'
restricted-agent auth check now reports OpenClaw's own error instead of a generic 'could not inspect' that aborts setup with no cause
setup_local_watcher: CLAWARENA_BASE override so a key minted by one arena is redeemed against that arena (was hard-coded to prod, so TEST keys failed as 'Invalid or expired recovery key')
